item.description:
Copas 1.0.2

The clipboard board is now two panes. Everything you have copied runs down the left, newest first and still grouped by day, and the whole of whichever clip you are on is shown beside it. Nothing is truncated any more — it is either in the list or in the pane next to it.

  • Arrows turn ninety degrees with the layout. Up and down move between clips, and Option with them jumps a whole day at a time. Page Up and Page Down move a screenful. Left and right go back to the search field, where they belong.
  • The mouse works too. Click a clip to read it, double-click to paste it.
  • Search marks what it found in the full text on the right, not only in the list — so a match buried deep in a long clip is visible rather than merely counted.

Fixed

  • Settings now opens. It never did: the window macOS was asked for is only ever shown for apps that keep a Dock icon, and the request reported success regardless, so the menu item did nothing at all and said nothing about it. Settings is now a window Copas builds itself, and ⌘W closes it.

Your clips, settings and shortcuts are untouched by this update.

Copas 1.0.1

Copas has an icon. 1.0.0 shipped with the generic application placeholder in the Dock switcher, in Finder, and in the update sheet you are most likely reading this in.

Nothing else about the app has changed. Your clips, settings and shortcuts are untouched by this update.

Copas 1.0

The first release. A clipboard manager that lives in the menu bar: press ⇧⌘V and everything you have copied is a strip of cards under the menu bar, newest first, grouped by day. Arrow to one, press Return, and it pastes into whatever you were just typing in.

What it does

  • Keeps formatting. Copy something bold and it pastes back bold.
  • Search that reaches the whole clip, not just its first line — and the text inside your screenshots. Type anywhere on the board to start, or narrow it with app:xcode, type:image, has:text.
  • Reads text in images as they arrive, on your Mac, through Vision. A screenshot of a receipt is findable by what the receipt says.
  • ⇧⌘2 captures a region of the screen as text — a receipt, an error dialog, something somebody sent you as a picture.
  • Skips what it should. Anything a password manager marks as concealed is never read, never hashed, and never written to disk. Other apps can be excluded by hand.

Privacy

Everything stays on your Mac. No account, no sync, no analytics. Text recognition runs locally. The only network request Copas makes is to its own update feed.

Requirements

macOS 14 or later. Universal — Apple silicon and Intel. Signed and notarised by Apple.
